newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU sees Brcko ruling helping heal war wounds.
newsitem.headline: EU sees Brcko ruling helping heal war wounds.

text.p: The European Union said an arbitration ruling last Friday on the disputed Bosnian town of Brcko should help to heal the wounds of war over time.

In a statement issued over the weekend by the EU's Dutch presidency, the union said it would assist the process set in motion by the ruling, adding however that the co-operation of all Bosnian parties was essential to its success.

U.S. arbiter Roberts Owen ruled on Friday that Brcko, claimed by both Serbs and the Moslem-Croat federation, would be put under international supervision pending a final decision next year on its status.
Brcko, a Sava River port considered one of the region's main flashpoints, was captured by Bosnian Serbs early in the 1992-95 war and purged of its mainly Moslem-Croat pre-war population.
Serbs had threatened to resume war if they were denied control of the town, but the federation said handing Brcko to the Serbs would reward ethnic cleansing.
The EU said the arbitration decision would fill the last gap of the peace agreement that was left open.
"The decision sets in motion a process which should help to heal the wounds of war over time," it said in a statement.
The statement said the EU and its member states would assist the high representative and his deputy for Brcko in guiding this process and implementing the goals of the arbitral decision.
Of particular importance were the principle of freedom of movement, implementation of the results of the local elections this summer and the principle of return of displaced persons and refugees.
"The full cooperation of all Bosnian parties will be essential to the success of this process," the EU said.

"It will also need the support of the international community both in terms of personnel and finances. Assistance in the field of police, economic reconstruction and housing is of particular importance."
On Friday, the United States welcomed the ruling and also called on rival factions to cooperate with the decision.
